Class Comprehension Binder

The primitive class comprehension binder { x | 𝛗 } (also denoted κ) forms the class of all sets x : Class satisfying syntactic formula 𝛗 : Fm. All three tokens {, |, and } in a comprehension expression resolve to this single binder symbol.

How to Understand It

Kernel AST & Logical Specification of Class Comprehension:

  • SML AST Constructor (in ClassTerm / Class_p, typetheory.ML:554): HC (CpKappa of 'Class_Truth_FUNEX) where 'Class_Truth_FUNEX = Fm_LBound_id (LBound_id (LVariable_id vx, phi)).
  • Constructor Arguments (Arity 1 higher-order binder / 2 syntactic components):
    1. Bound variable x : Variable (ranging over default object type Class; never Set),
    2. Comprehension matrix / formula body 𝛗 : Fm (= Bool.Expression).
  • Metatype / Signature: (Variable × Fm) → Class.Expression (or higher-order binder signature (Class → Bool) → Class).
  • Symbol Classification: Binder (variable-binding class-forming functional symbol). Clicking {, |, or } in {x | 𝛗} always navigates to this single symbol page.
  • Defining Axiom & Rule: Governed by RulClassComprehension (3.01) and AxmMetaClassComprehension (4.06), printed in full below.
